steps.text: Combine beer and onion slices in a large pot; bring to a boil.
Add bratwurst, pepper flakes, garlic powder, salt, and pepper to beer and onion mixture. Reduce heat to medium and cook for 10 to 12 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat and lightly oil the grate.
Transfer bratwurst to a plate. Reduce heat to low and let onions simmer until needed.

Cook bratwurst on the preheated grill, turning occasionally to get char marks, until no longer pink in the middle, 5 to 10 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 160 degrees F (70 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Beer Brats
raw_recipe.description: Brats are simmered with onions and spices in beer for fantastic flavor, then finished up on the grill for a perfectly crispy, charred exterior.

video.description: Two great things in one delicious meal! Beer, onions, and brats go hand in hand for this kind of meal!

review.reviewBody: I made this as a try out run to see if I'd want to serve it for guests this weekend. I halved the recipe since it was for just 3 of us. It was all gone and I only had one. I could have eaten at least 3 easily and that says a lot! Great recipe! I followed the recipe and did not change a thing. The spiciness was very good. I may take it up a notch when I serve it to my guests who happen to like spicy food. Just an f.y.i. though... without the sauce it isn't very hot for those who may not like heat. Thank you Zach!

Made this for our annual Oktoberfest gathering. Cooked 35 Denmark Foods Arizona Fresh all natural bratwurst. I used Guinness Stout Draft (only 5 cans were necessary because the brats took up so much space in my Dutch oven). Simmered them on low for 30 minutes. Used only double the amount of the dry spices even though I tripled the amount of brats. We grilled them on a propane grill. Served with options of warm currywurst sauce (18 ingredients!), various sauerkrauts, and a “mustard bar.” Had both hoagie rolls and pretzel rolls. Everyone had fun making various flavor combinations, but the brats could easily stand alone with nothing extra needed!
I love Beer Brats. One of the things we do though is reverse the order. We grill the Brats first, then boil them in beer. This causes them to be juicier and more full. Everything else was great.

Awesome brats! Slight modification using 2 packages (total of 14 brats)...
- used 6 bottles of Yuengling Black & Tan beer (adds great flavor) and 1 cup water
- poked slight holes in each brat before boiling (flavor of beer seeps inside brats)
- after finished boiling, throw on grill on low heat to brown the brats
- after removing from grill, put right back into the pot of beer...that way, the skin on brats don't start shriveling and drying up...keeps the brats nice and juicy!
Family and friends love these...always request to keep making them!!

Juicy and well cooked! Made some tweaks instead though. We marinated them overnight in Pilsners instead of parboiling them and then grilled them outside for 20-25 min at 350 degrees on the grill. Goes great with Jaeger Spaetzle, sauerkraut, and dijon!

I’ve been using this recipe for over a year now. Love! I make great use of the beer by reducing it to an au jus. If you plan to reduce, always pick a lighter beer. Dark beers are great for flavoring the brat, but will usually NOT make an edible au jus. Bun not required It’s completely devoured here, so I always have to double the recipe.

This was super tasty! I really liked how the brats came out, super juicy and with a great snap in the casing. I made exactly as written. However, I found the texture of the onions a bit off-putting, so the ones I didn't eat I kept reducing in a skillet with the remaining liquid, to get that carmelized texture that I love (onion Beer Candy!). And perhaps some suggested beer types would be in order. I used a Hazy IPA that I had on hand, and while it was tasty, not everyone would appreciate the hoppiness. Anone else try different beers? What has everyone tried and liked? Maybe Zach can publish an update with a list of beers reviewers have tried and loved?
These brats were delicious. When I say I want a brat, this is the one. I finished them in an iron skillet then threw the onions in to carmelize them. Perfect.

YESTERDAY: I’ll add caraway seeds, delete red pepper flakes, and finally brown on the stove top in a cast iron grill pan. Sauerkraut and mustard on top, maybe potato salad on the side. BUT TODAY: I’m making Slow Cooker Beer Brats recipe from Tasting Table. It includes baby gold potatoes, onions, sauerkraut, garlic, bay leaves, and caraway + mustard seeds. I’m adding carrots and using Guinness (because it’s the only beer I like and I love a strong earthy flavor). Serving with chopped flat-leaf parsley on July 4, 2025 to celebrate America’s birthday! P.S. DON’T PIERCE THE BRATS! That way the flavors leech out of the meat. Per dozens of recipes that I read.
I used 3 cans of Guinness. We don’t have a grill so I airfried them. They we delicious. Served them with the onions, brown mustard and sauerkraut!

Not bad...not bad at all. I'm not usually a huge fan of brauts but these turned out pretty darn good. I used the cheapest beer I had on hand, 2 cans of Coors Light and used a jumbo pack of 12 Johnsonville beer brats. I also doubled the onions. Tossed everything in a slow cooker and let it sit for about 4 hours. I took the brats out of the "beer bath" and cooked them on low on the grill. This gave them better color, if not they don't look very appetizing. The grilling also gave it a little sweetness. I also took the onions out of the "beer bath" and sauteed a little to carmelized. Hubby liked them pretty well, but to my surprise my picky eater gobbled it up.

Absolutely delicious! Very familiar with Wisconsin brats, this cooking method with spices takes brats up a whole 'nother level! I used 4 cans of high quality gluten free beer (guest has celiac disease) for 15 brats, and one onion would be enough.
Excellent!

It was too hot today (America's 250th Anniversary) to do a cook out, so we made this beer brat recipe instead: it was so good! As someone else suggested, we simmered the brats in the beer for 30 minutes (not 10-12) because I wasn't sure I trusted my panini press to cook the brats thoroughly: they came out great. Will definitely make again.

I have simmered brats in beer and onions for 30 minutes before grilling them to finish the exterior. It softens the skin for more pleasurable eating. For 5 Johnsonville original brats, I use 3 cans of beer and sliced onion to what looks good. Bring to a boil and remove the scum as it accumulates, and once it is at a gentle boil turn down the heat and simmer so that the total cooking time equals 30 minutes. Remove from heat and plate the brats and let the hubby finish them on the grill. (Of course, he gets all the credit for being such a grill master, lol). We were given this brat cooking method by one of our employees back in the mid 1990's and I have been doing it ever since. If you want no spice and easy prep, this is the way to go.

I've made beer brats for years! Im just curious as to why no one seems to be adding German Sweet &Sour Red Cabbage as a side?? My husband's Grandmother served red cabbage with all holiday meals, Sundays after church, beer brats days with German potato salad as well as the red cabbage! We probably have brats for dinner once a month in the cold months and at least weekly during the warm months! Sauerkrat and red cabbage are a requirement!!
We did not have onions in the house so I ended up using fresh shishitos. And this created a wonderful new flavor.
Tastes good and easy, plus customizable!
This is a crowd pleaser for sure! This will be the only beer brat recipe you will ever need.
This recipe is great! The brats are flavor and the recipe is so easy. It was an easy weekday dinner.
